# Urdu voice notes

- Everyday spoken Urdu, warm and conversational, the way a good storyteller talks; not
  literary or formal Urdu. Prefer common words over Persian/Arabic-heavy vocabulary.
- Common English loanwords people actually say are fine (فون، پولیس، پلان).
- Keep the storyteller register: "وہ", "اسے", "لیکن", "تو", "جب تک". Never "اور پھر".
- Character and place names stay as they are spoken in the film, written in Urdu script.
- Numbers and years as spoken words.
- Same rhythm rules as English: short punches mixed with longer lines; the twist alone.
- The closing question addresses the viewer as "آپ".
